knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Values of Trigonometric Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula

question.:question/problem:
Without using a calculator, find the **exact** value.

$$
\cos^2\left(105^\circ\right)-\sin^2\left(105^\circ\right)
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the cosine double-angle identity:

$$
\cos^2\left(x\right)-\sin^2\left(x\right)=\cos(2x)
$$

Substitute the angle and evaluate the standard-angle cosine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\cos^2\left(105^\circ\right)-\sin^2\left(105^\circ\right) \\
&= \cos\left(2\cdot 105^\circ\right) \\
&= \cos\left(210^\circ\right) \\
&= -\cos\left(30^\circ\right) \\
&= -\frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

knowledge_point.title: Finding Exact Values of Trigonometric Expressions Using the Double-Angle Formula

question.:question/worked-solution:
Let $E$ denote the expression in the question. Recognize the expanded perfect square:

$$
\begin{aligned}
E &= \left(\cos^2\left(112.5^\circ\right)-\sin^2\left(112.5^\circ\right)\right)^2
\end{aligned}
$$

Use the cosine double-angle identity:

$$
\cos^2\left(x\right)-\sin^2\left(x\right)=\cos(2x)
$$

Substitute the angle and evaluate the standard-angle cosine:

$$
\begin{aligned}
&\cos^2\left(112.5^\circ\right)-\sin^2\left(112.5^\circ\right) \\
&= \cos\left(2\cdot 112.5^\circ\right) \\
&= \cos\left(225^\circ\right) \\
&= -\cos\left(45^\circ\right) \\
&= -\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, square the value:

$$
\begin{aligned}
E &= \left(-\frac{\sqrt{2}}{2}\right)^2 \\
&= \frac{1}{2}
\end{aligned}
$$
